query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adopting an enhanced adaptive free-energy sampling method—such as a metadynamics-assisted adaptive thermodynamic integration scheme—will substantially reduce the computational cost of obtaining accurate fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties in multicomponent high-entropy systems while faithfully retaining vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration coupling contributions.
generation.material_initial_state: Elemental, binary, and multicomponent high-entropy alloy systems in both the solid and liquid (fusion regime) states.
generation.intervention: Replace full-scale explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy evaluations with an integrated enhanced sampling framework that couples metadynamics and adaptive thermodynamic integration.
generation.conditions: High-temperature conditions near the fusion point for alloys ranging from elemental and binary systems to more compositionally complex high-entropy systems.
generation.structural_mediator: Efficient exploration of the free energy landscape, enabling capture of rare phase transition events and retaining detailed entropy contributions (vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration coupling).
generation.mechanism: The intervention accelerates phase space sampling by biasing the system to overcome free-energy barriers, thereby reducing the number of necessary ab initio evaluations. This efficient integration of enhanced sampling techniques minimizes computational overhead compared to traditional molecular dynamics while preserving the accuracy of entropy-related contributions.
generation.predicted_outcome: A significant decrease in computational cost (potentially an order-of-magnitude reduction) with comparable fidelity to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics outcomes and improved scaling over methods like TOR-TILD when applied to multicomponent systems.
generation.baseline: Current explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics approaches and TOR-TILD workflows, which accurately compute free energies but are computationally demanding and slow for complex high-entropy systems.
generation.boundary: The method is expected to perform effectively in the fusion regime (near melting temperatures) for systems up to high-entropy alloys. Its performance and accuracy beyond these compositional and temperature ranges remain to be validated.
generation.uncertainty: The precise speedup and fidelity retention depend on the system’s complexity and the adequacy of the sampling method to capture all relevant entropy contributions. There is uncertainty whether all rare event dynamics, especially in extremely multicomponent mixtures, are fully resolved.

falsification_experiment.design: Apply the proposed enhanced adaptive sampling method to a representative high-entropy alloy system at temperatures near its fusion point. Compare the computed free energy differences and entropy contributions (vibrational, anharmonic, electron–vibration coupling) for both solid and liquid phases with those obtained from full-scale explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD. Measure the computational time and accuracy across these methods.
measurements: Computed free energy differences between phases
Quantitative vibrational and anharmonic entropy contributions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the enhanced sampling method fails to reproduce free energy and entropy values within an acceptable error margin relative to full ab initio MD (or does not retain key entropy differences) or if the computational cost is not significantly reduced compared to TOR-TILD, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The extremely harsh environment of the high temperature plasma imposes strict requirements on the construction materials of the first wall in a fusion reactor. In this work, a refractory alloy system, WTaVTiZrx, with low activation and high entropy, was theoretically designed based on semi-empirical formula and produced using a laser cladding method. The effects of Zr proportions on the metallographic microstructure, phase composition, and alloy chemistry of a high-entropy alloy cladding layer were investigated using a metallographic microscope, XRD (X-ray diffraction), SEM (scanning electron microscope), and EDS (energy dispersive spectrometer), respectively. The high-entropy alloys have a single-phase BCC structure, and the cladding layers exhibit a typical dendritic microstructure feature. The evolution of microstructure and mechanical properties of the high-entropy alloys, with respect to annealing temperature, was studied to reveal the performance stability of the alloy at a high temperature. High or medium- entropy alloys (HEAs/MEAs) are multi-principal element alloys with equal atomic elemental composition, some of which have shown record-breaking mechanical performance. However, the link between short-range order (SRO) and the exceptional mechanical properties of these alloys has remained elusive. The local destruction of SRO by dislocation glide has been predicted to lead to a rejuvenated state with increased entropy and free energy, creating softer zones within the matrix and planar fault boundaries that enhance the ductility, but this has not been verified. Here, we integrate in situ nanomechanical testing with energy-filtered four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) and directly observe the rejuvenation during cyclic mechanical loading in single crystal CrCoNi at room temperature. Surprisingly, stacking faults (SFs) and twin boundaries (TBs) are reversible in initial cycles but become irreversible after a thousand cycles, indicating SF energy reduction and rejuvenation. While first-principles methods have been successfully applied to characterize individual properties of multi-principal element alloys (MPEA), their use in searching for optimal trade-offs between competing properties is hampered by high computational demands. In this work, we present a framework to explore Pareto-optimal compositions by integrating advanced ab initio-based techniques into a Bayesian multi-objective optimization workflow, complemented by a simple analytical model providing straightforward analysis of trends. We benchmark the framework by applying it to solid solution strengthening and ductility of refractory MPEAs, with the parameters of the strengthening and ductility models being efficiently computed using a combination of the coherent-potential approximation method, accounting for finite-temperature effects, and actively-learned moment-tensor potentials parameterized with ab initio data.
